target_intervention_label: Gating workup: fitness/organ function plus HLA class I typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping, CD33/CD123 density, TP53 variant-level NGS
comment: Ranking a lab requisition first is a category error, and her own concern row concedes the point: peripheral blasts went 58% to 82% inside a fortnight, so this workup runs alongside cycle 1 of nct:NCT04050280 rather than in front of it. The gates she names are real, CD33 on at least 20% of blasts and a measured ejection fraction, and both get answered by a screening visit that costs a phone call and a send-out. Ordering it as pick 1 spends a therapeutic slot on the one thing nobody at this table opposes.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells (Bleakley/HighPassBio platform, NCT03326921)
comment: She is right that the case was submitted for this and right that the genotype retrieval starts this week, but rank 1 asks nine patients on a feasibility-and-DLT primary endpoint to carry an 85% marrow. Mazziotta gave an A*02:01-restricted TCR to post-transplant disease and got median OS 242 days with only 2 of 15 carrying overt disease (pmid:40473616), and Medigene's own reading of their phase 1 was that tumour burden was the limiting factor (pmid:41008812). Collection, manufacture and lymphodepletion take weeks that a marrow moving this fast may not give her, which is why I want this third rather than off the list.

target_intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123-directed ADC)
comment: Taking pick 4 rather than his transplant pick, because the veno-occlusive line is hardening into a hepatic veto and Daver does not support that: both dose-limiting events occurred at 0.180 and 0.450 mg/kg, four to ten times the 0.045 mg/kg recommended phase 2 dose, and both were reversible (pmid:38423051). That is a dose-level finding rather than a property of the drug, so striking CD123 out of the pre-conditioning window on it is an over-read. Where he is right is the interval: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) on 29 patients is too soft to displace CLAG-GO as the cytoreduction, so hold it as the fallback if CD33 density comes back low.

target_intervention_label: Rezatapopt (PC14586) + azacitidine on NCT06616636, contingent on a TP53 Y220C call
comment: Her rank 1 is my rank 1, so I am taking pick 5, which fails on my terms before it fails on hers: Carter restored wild-type p53 conformation in Y220C AML and got limited or no apoptosis unless venetoclax or an MDM2/XPO1 partner was added (pmid:40608889), and venetoclax is what she just progressed through. An azacitidine backbone on nct:NCT06616636 keeps the half of the mechanism that does not kill, and the trial's own CLIA gate of Y220C above 2% VAF sits at the detection limit of the panel that called her TP53-negative. If the variant comes back Y220C I would chase an MDM2 or XPO1 combination instead of listing a contingent pick that resolves to a failed drug.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells (Bleakley/HighPassBio platform, NCT03326921)
comment: We rank the same product four places apart, and the disagreement is about what runs first. Fludarabine/cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion into an 85% marrow, in a series that reported grade 3-5 infections and one grade 4 infusion reaction in 9 patients, is a myelosuppressive step being ordered with no creatinine clearance, no LFTs and no ejection fraction anywhere in the chart. The missing safety datum I want named rather than gestured at is that nobody in NCT03326921 was infused after a second allograft, so the HCT2 interaction is unmeasured; this is a dissent and not a veto, because the cells themselves produced no DLT, no CRS and no ICANS and preferences.json vetoes nothing, but I would not put lymphodepletion ahead of cytoreduction.

target_intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123-directed ADC), off-label after the May 2026 BPDCN approval
comment: Targeting rank 4 rather than the second-graft platform at rank 1, which I support and gate the same way they do. Two dose-limiting veno-occlusive events in 68 patients is the wrong hepatic exposure in the weeks before a conditioning regimen, so the dissent is against the pre-conditioning window rather than against the drug: if HCT2 comes off the table, pivekimab at rank 4 stands. The consistency I owe the board is that I ranked another calicheamicin conjugate second, and the reason is Taksin's 57 patients at 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7 with no grade 3-4 hepatic toxicity and no veno-occlusive disease, seven of them transplanted afterwards; pivekimab has no comparable pre-transplant hepatic series.

target_intervention_label: 211At-BC8-B10 (astatine-211 anti-CD45) targeted conditioning + allogeneic HCT, NCT03670966
comment: Withdrawing the veto I pre-registered, cleanly: it was conditioned on a rank-1 pick taking her to conditioning at 85% blasts on the strength of Iomab-B, and at rank 5, with human efficacy for 211At-BC8-B10 stated as nil and the null OS (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.70-1.41) sitting in their own concern list, the condition is not met. What survives is a dissent on transportability, because SIERRA excluded prior allo-HCT and NCT03670966 wants a haploidentical relative rather than the sibling who gave the 2020 graft, so the randomised 17.1% still cannot be quoted for her at any rank. On the workup, they are right that it is a prerequisite and not a therapy, and I concede the rank while holding the substance: CD33 on at least 20% of blasts is a screening gate on their own rank-1 trial and the qualitative flow result does not clear it.

target_intervention_label: Rezatapopt (PC14586) + azacitidine on NCT06616636, contingent on a TP53 Y220C call
comment: Ranked fifth on a Y220C call that does not exist in either direction, and NCT06616636 screens at VAF above 2% on the same class of panel that returned her TP53 result, so the assay would decide eligibility before the biology does. Carter's work has reactivated Y220C p53 restoring wild-type conformation with limited or absent apoptosis unless venetoclax is added, which is the agent she progressed through, so a positive call still leaves the pick without a partner drug and no peer-reviewed effect size to price it against. Their gemtuzumab reading I accept rather than argue with, absent from the NCCN poor-risk induction options while present for favourable and intermediate, and it lands on my own rank 2 as squarely as on theirs.

target_intervention_label: Gating workup before any therapeutic commitment: fitness and organ-function documentation plus HLA class I typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient and sibling donor, quantitative CD33/CD123 antigen density, and TP53 variant-level NGS
comment: This is the one rank-1 on the board that reads her free text back accurately, and conservative flagging its own thresholds as "mine and not hers" against an empty toxicity_vetoes list is exactly the right handling. My qualification is about how it renders: a workup at rank 1 will read to her as wait, and conservative's own first concern says it runs alongside cytoreduction, so that sentence has to survive into the PI rather than the rank number. One item inside that workup is not like the others: HA-1 genotyping of her and the sibling carries a manufacturing lead time nothing else on the list does, so it belongs on the same day as the ejection fraction and not after a response is documented.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells (Bleakley/HighPassBio platform), NCT03326921
comment: Taking their rank 3 rather than their rank 1, because that is the pick where they answer me. On the registered endpoint they are right and I wrote the same thing in round 1: NCT03326921 is powered for manufacturing feasibility and DLT, 4 of 9 is a descriptive secondary, and nobody should quote 44.4% to her as a response rate. Where I still hold is narrower than my rank 1 was: n=9 on a feasibility endpoint limits what may be claimed, not whether HLA-A*02:01 gets retrieved from a 2020 chart, and critic's own concern list lands in the same place when it calls the option a hypothesis rather than a plan.

target_intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF + fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
comment: I came in at rank 1 on the TCR-T and this is the position that moved me: pmid 40473616 and pmid 41008812 are tumour-burden arguments rather than evidence-tier ones, and a T-cell product that cannot work at 85% blasts serves the stated request while failing the stated goal, which is curative intent. Cytoreduction first is what keeps the HLA-restricted door open, and NCT04050280 does it inside a trial, which satisfies prefers_trials rather than trading against it. The condition I attach is that the HLA record pull and the HA-1 genotyping of her and the sibling run during induction, because holding them until a response is documented restarts the manufacturing clock at the exact moment the window is best.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T (donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells, Bleakley platform) on NCT03326921
comment: I agree with their rank 1, so I am taking their rank 4. Guideline silence is doing too much work here: concensusite writes that NCCN carries no DLI recommendation at all and then ranks DLI above the option this run was submitted to find. free_text_constraints names HLA-restricted immunotherapy eligibility as the explicit reason for the case and asks for that pathway to be surfaced and de-risked, and the de-risking step is a records request for an allele-level report that was already run in 2020.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells (Bleakley/HighPassBio platform, NCT03326921)
comment: Rank 1 is what I dissent from, not the option itself. The registered primary endpoint of NCT03326921 is manufacturing feasibility and dose-limiting toxicity, so 4 of 9 is a descriptive secondary readout from a trial never powered to produce a response rate, and the denominator mixes patients whose CR was induced with patients whose CR was maintained (pmid:38683966). Your own concern row says nobody should hear 4 of 9 as a response rate, and I agree; thin evidence labelled honestly still beats no option, but putting it above the cytoreduction that makes it deliverable is a separate claim and the n=9 does not support it.

target_intervention_label: 211At-BC8-B10 (astatine-211 anti-CD45) targeted conditioning + allogeneic HCT, NCT03670966
comment: Taking rank 5 rather than rank 1, since your own CLAG-GO concern row already concedes that the 56.6% belongs to CLAG-M plus lintuzumab-Ac225 and not to CLAG-GO. SIERRA hit its registered primary endpoint at durable CR 17.1% (9.4-27.5) versus 0%, and in that same trial overall survival did not move (HR 0.99, 0.70-1.41, p=0.96), the FDA declined the filing and asked for an OS study, and prior allo-HCT was an exclusion, so she sits outside the randomised population (pmid:39298738); 211At-BC8-B10 then inherits the principle with no human efficacy behind it at all, only a syngeneic mouse transplant using a murine anti-CD45 (pmid:23471305). One more from your notes: the 47% flotetuzumab figure in TP53-abnormal disease is a post-hoc correlative read on 15 patients with no CI reported (pmid:33057635), so it should stay where you put it and travel no further.

target_intervention_label: Gating workup before any therapeutic commitment (organ function, HLA class I typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping, CD33/CD123 density, TP53 variant-level NGS)
comment: The gating logic holds where it is specific: NCT04050280 screens on CD33 in at least 20% of blasts, and profile.json carries no creatinine clearance, no LFTs and no ejection fraction, so most of the toxicity talk on this board is currently unpriced. A workup is not a therapy, though, and ranking it first leaves the ranking question open in a patient whose peripheral blasts went 58% to 82% inside a fortnight, which your own first concern concedes. Run the assays as a parallel track and let rank 1 name something that treats her.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2), sibling or alternative donor, after cytoreduction
comment: Your finding that no NCCN category attaches to HCT2 after post-transplant relapse is correct and the board should hear it, and it does not lower my rank 1. What sits behind HCT2 is four registries agreeing on one stratification (pmid:26367221 n=2632, pmid:17909197 n=399, pmid:22167752 n=263, pmid:23918951 n=179), which replicates a prognostic model rather than a treatment effect, and none of them adjusts for who gets selected into a second graft; a missing category number is not missing evidence, and evidence quality is not the same axis as clinical value. Separately on your rank 5: NCT06616636 wants a CLIA Y220C call at VAF above 2%, which sits at the detection limit of the same panel that called her TP53-negative, so the assay rather than the biology may decide that eligibility.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells (Bleakley/HighPassBio platform, NCT03326921)
comment: No guideline lists HA-1 TCR-T. The route is a different story: NCCN AML v3.2026 puts clinical trial first for relapsed/refractory disease and its workup already orders the high-resolution HLA typing this pick is waiting on, so pursuing NCT03326921 is guideline-concordant care. What I cannot square with any guideline text is the rank, because everything pointing cellular therapy at post-transplant relapse assumes cytoreduced disease and the 4 of 9 in pmid:38683966 mixes induced with maintained remissions, so keep the records request moving this week and the infusion itself behind the debulking.

target_intervention_label: Gating workup: fitness and organ-function documentation plus HLA class I typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping, antigen density, TP53 variant-level NGS
comment: Ranking the workup first has real guideline cover: the NCCN AML v3.2026 evaluation includes HLA typing for anyone in whom allogeneic HCT is considered, liver and renal chemistries, and cardiac assessment where cardiotoxic exposure sits in the history, which FLAG-IDA put there. The one item no guideline orders is HA-1 genotyping at rs1801284, so sending it through the NCT03326921 screening pathway is the right call rather than a workaround. The concurrency framing matters too, since nothing in the workup list licenses waiting on results while peripheral blasts run from 58% to 82%.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) on a cytoreduce-first platform, sibling or alternative donor
comment: No NCCN category and no ELN grade attaches to a second allograft after post-transplant relapse; the pathways assume a first transplant, so all five of us are ranking HCT2 on registry evidence (pmid:26367221) where the guideline text stops, and the PI should read that as uncovered rather than contraindicated. I rank HCT2 second myself, so this is a qualification of placement, not of the pick. NCCN AML v3.2026 (the 11/24/2025 text, the floor I could verify) and ELN 2022 (pmid:35797463) both describe cytoreduction and then transplant, and critic's own blast-gate concern concedes that ordering, which argues against rank 1.

target_intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF + fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
comment: Same rank-1 as mine, and for TP53-aberrant poor-risk AML NCCN v3.2026 lists clinical trial and nothing else, so a trial regimen leading the board is the guideline position rather than a workaround. My reservation is which component does the work: the same guideline lists gemtuzumab for R/R CD33-positive AML with no cytogenetic qualifier yet keeps it out of the poor-risk induction options it offers favourable and intermediate risk, and ALFA-0701 enrolled de novo disease only (pmid:22482940) while hers is MDS-related. The guideline-fit case rests on the CLAG backbone plus NCT04050280's population match, and the 56.6% composite CR belongs to lintuzumab-Ac225's payload (pmid:39955432), which should not migrate onto this regimen.
